[USER] User is interested in accessing rehabilitation services from remote or rural areas.  
[USER] User is inquiring about affordable or subsidized options for rehabilitation services.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tele-rehabilitation involves using telecommunication technologies such as video conferencing, messaging, and phone calls to connect patients with rehabilitation specialists.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Mobile rehabilitation services involve healthcare professionals and therapists traveling to remote or rural areas to provide rehabilitation services.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Community-based rehabilitation programs can be delivered at the community level with the help of community health workers, volunteers, and family members.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Medicare provides coverage for some rehabilitation services for people over 65 years of age, people with disabilities, and those with end-stage renal diseases.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Medicaid provides coverage for some rehabilitation services for low-income families and children with disabilities.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Many private health insurance plans cover rehabilitation services, but the extent of coverage varies.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some states provide rehabilitation services through their departments of health or social services, with eligibility criteria applying.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some non-profit organizations provide rehabilitation services to low-income populations or people living in remote or rural areas, which may be free or low-cost.  
[USER] User is asking about specific types of rehabilitation services that can be accessed through tele-rehabilitation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tele-rehabilitation can include physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and mental health counseling.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tele-rehabilitation has been used for conditions such as strokes, spinal cord injuries, traumatic brain injuries, neuromuscular disorders, and mental health conditions.  
[USER] User is concerned about the effectiveness of tele-rehabilitation compared to in-person rehabilitation services.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tele-rehabilitation can be as effective as in-person care for improving functional outcomes and quality of life for various conditions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tele-rehabilitation can reduce healthcare costs by eliminating travel time and expenses for patients.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Limitations of tele-rehabilitation include the need for hands-on techniques for certain conditions and the lack of sensory feedback.  
[USER] User expresses concern about the potential awkwardness of therapy sessions over video chat and the ability to connect with the therapist.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Many patients report feeling connected and comfortable with remote therapy sessions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tele-rehabilitation technology has evolved to provide interactive experiences, including screen sharing and chat functionalities.
